title: integrated-ops-toolkit-access-to-travel-2029
author: Priya Singh
body:
Overview
=======
This document is a single, practical toolkit combining company-wide procedures and forms for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel policies. It is designed for cross-functional teams (engineering, finance, security, people-ops) to follow a consistent, auditable process. Use the templates and checklists below when opening requests or executing approvals.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Relevant for hosted, dedicated, and private deployment engagements.
- Auditable by Security and Finance during reviews and audits.

Goals
-----
- Reduce approval latency for low-risk requests while enforcing controls for regulated activities.
- Provide templates that standardize requests and vendor assessments.
- Ensure data handling and retention align with classification levels.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy custodianship).
- Operational owners: Security (access, data classification), Eng-SRE (change runbooks), Procurement (vendor onboarding).
- Escalation path: requestor -> requestor's manager -> owner_team lead -> Head of Finance/Head of Security as required.

Quick reference: decision matrix
--------------------------------
| Area | Low risk (auto/manager) | Medium risk (2 approvers) | High risk (committee) |
| Access to internal services | Manager approval | Security + Manager | Security Committee |
| Change to runtime infra | N/A | Eng-sre + Product | Emergency CAB |
| Vendor procurement (<= $25k) | Procurement manager | Procurement + Finance | Legal + Exec |
| Travel reimbursement (<= $1,000) | Manager approval | Finance + Manager | Exec approval |

Access & permissions procedure
------------------------------
1) Request initiation
   - Use the Access Request template in the Request Tracker (confluence link: /requests/access).
   - Required fields: service name (e.g. redwood-control-plane, serving-runtime), role requested, business justification, data access level.
2) Data classification check
   - Classify data involved: PUBLIC | INTERNAL | RESTRICTED | REGULATED. See Data Management section for retention and handling rules.
3) Approval and provisioning
   - Low risk: manager approves in the Request Tracker; IAM ticket is auto-created and provisioned by platform-auth bot (approx latency: 4 hours).
   - Medium/high risk: Security review completed within 2 business days. Provisioning requires documented justification and an expiration (default 90 days unless otherwise approved).
4) Post-provision audit
   - Automated weekly IAM delta report to owners; access with no activity for 60 days is flagged for review.

Example IAM policy snippet (apply via platform-auth CLI):

# Grant read-access to embeddings store
policy: |
  version: 1
  statement:
    - effect: allow
      action: ["kv:Read", "object:Get"]
      resource: "arn:redwood:storage:us-west-2:account:embeddings/*"
      condition: { "StringEquals": { "redwood:Role": "ml-researcher" } }

Change management (engineering systems)
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Minimize service disruption while enabling frequent, auditable deployments.

Change categories
- Standard change: pre-approved, repeatable (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal change: requires review and scheduled window.
- Emergency change: applied outside normal windows; post-facto CAB review required.

Procedure (normal change)
1) Create a Change Request ticket in CHANGE-BOARD with: summary, impact analysis, rollback plan, monitoring playbook, owner, and target window.
2) Peer review: two engineers (one from owning service) review design.
3) Security review if data-scope includes RESTRICTED/REGULATED.
4) Canaries: deploy to 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Metrics to monitor: latency p50/p95, error rate, token throughput, KV cache hit rate.
5) Full rollout: expand in windows (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated health gates.
6) Post-deploy: complete change ticket with metrics and retrospective if SLO breach or unexpected errors.

Telemetry gates (example thresholds)
| Metric | Canary threshold | Full rollout threshold |
| error_rate | < 0.5% | < 0.7% |
| p95_latency | < 800ms | < 1.2s |

Rollback steps (if threshold exceeded)
1) Trigger automated rollback: revert to previous model revision or config snapshot.
2) Notify oncall via PagerDuty runbook for serving-runtime.
3) Open postmortem within 48 hours if rollback occurred.

Data management: classification and retention
-------------------------------------------
Classification levels and handling rules:
- PUBLIC: No restrictions. Retention: business default.
- INTERNAL: Access by employees only. Retention: 2 years default unless specified.
- RESTRICTED: Encrypt at rest with customer KMS, access-by-approval; retention: 7 years for auditable datasets.
- REGULATED: Subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., GDPR/CCPA financial/personal data). Retention: per contract.

Data retention policy examples
| Data type | Classification | Default retention | Owner |
| logs (application) | INTERNAL | 365 days | Eng-SRE |
| customer-audit-logs | REGULATED | 7 years | Security + Finance |
| embeddings derived from customer data | RESTRICTED | contract dependent | Research + Legal |

Procurement and vendor management
---------------------------------
Procurement thresholds & approvers:
- <= $2,500: Team budget owner sign-off (submit PR in Procurement system).
- $2,500–$25,000: Procurement + Finance approval.
- > $25,000: Legal review + Exec sponsor.

Vendor onboarding checklist
1) Business case and budget entry.
2) Security questionnaire (SSQ) completed: must score > 75% for low risk.
3) Contract template: use Standard SaaS Agreement (procurement library).
4) Data processing addendum (DPA) required if vendor handles RESTRICTED/REGULATED data.
5) KMS/HSM integration review if vendor will hold keys.
6) Insurance and SOC2 evidence collected.
7) Operational contacts & escalation list captured in vendor record.

Vendor scorecard fields (example)
- Security posture (SOC2, encryption)
- Data residency and compliance (regions, DPA)
- Financial stability (3-year run rate)
- Support SLAs and escalation channels
- Price & terms (TCO, termination)

Templates (to copy into the Procurement system)
- Vendor Scorecard CSV: vendor_name,security_score,dpa_required,annual_cost,sla_hours
- Contract clause snippet for data returns: "Upon termination, vendor will securely delete or return all customer data within 30 days and certify deletion."

Travel and expenses policy (concise)
-----------------------------------
Principles:
- Be economical; default to economy-class travel for flights < 6 hours.
- Use preferred vendors and booking portal for company rates.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.

Travel approval flow
1) Submit Travel Request form with purpose, itinerary, estimated cost, and approver (manager).
2) Travel > $1,000 requires Finance review. International travel with customer data access requires Security sign-off.
3) After travel: submit Expense Report with receipts within 7 business days. Expenses older than 30 days require CFO approval.

Per diem and limits (examples)
| Item | Limit | Notes |
| Meals | $75/day domestic | Higher for high-cost cities with prior approval |
| Lodging | $250/night domestic | Book in business rate; exceptions require manager approval |
| Ground transport | Actuals | Use shared rides when practical |

Expense templates and checklist
- Expense report fields: traveler, dates, client, purpose, line-item costs, receipts attached.
- Required receipt checklist: date, vendor, amount, card last4. Missing receipt action: manager justification + traveler attestation.

Audit & monitoring
------------------
- Monthly audit: Finance runs random sample of 5% of expense reports and 10% of vendor invoices.
- Quarterly access audit: Security reviews all accounts with RESTRICTED/REGULATED access.
- Change audit: Eng-SRE publishes quarterly change logs and incident rollups to the SRE dashboard.

Operational templates (copyable)
-------------------------------
1) Access Request (example text)
   - Summary: [one-line]
   - Service: [service name]
   - Role: [role]
   - Justification: [why access is needed]
   - Duration: [expiry date or permanent]
   - Data classification: [PUBLIC/INTERNAL/RESTRICTED/REGULATED]
2) Change Request (example text)
   - Summary, Impact, Rollback plan, Metrics to monitor, Owner, Rollout windows
3) Vendor Onboarding (example checklist)
   - Business case, SSQ score, DPA present, Contract signed, Escalation contacts
4) Travel Request (example text)
   - Traveler, Dates, Purpose, Estimated cost, Manager approver

Appendices
---------
A. Example change ticket template (markdown)
```
Title: [service] – [change short summary]
Owner: [name]
Impact: [high/medium/low]
Rollback: [steps]
Canary plan: [traffic %, duration, metrics]
Monitoring: [dashboard links]
```

B. Vendor SSQ highlights (key questions)
- Encryption at rest/in transit? KMS integration?
- SOC2 Type II? Last audit date?
- Data residency and subprocessors?

C. Contact matrix
- Finance: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security-ops@redwood.com
- Platform-auth (provisioning): platform-auth-bot@redwood.com
- Oncall (serving-runtime): pagerduty "serving-runtime"
